Metagame Health Map · power vs. popularity

Each legend plotted by how often it's played (x) against its match win rate (y). The shaded "watch zone" flags decks that are both genuinely popular and winning. The default threshold auto-adapts to each format/event — a deck must be >1 standard deviation above the mean in both play and win — and you can override it with the sliders. Set what counts as a deep run by match points. The Rounds toggle picks a match set — All = every match in the tournament, Day 1 = Day 1 matches only, Day 2 = Day 2 matches only — and both axes are computed over it: play rate = a legend's share of those matches, win rate = its record in them.

Watch zone = play ≥ 4.0% and win ≥ 56%
Deep run = ≥ 30 match points (W=3, D=1)
Assumptions & method
  • Win rate = tracked-vs-tracked matches only — both players submitted a decklist; byes, draws, and games against no-decklist drop-outs are excluded. The field is therefore an exact closed 50% system (50% = a genuinely average deck).
  • Play rate = a legend's share of tracked matches in the selected Rounds scope (All / Day 1 / Day 2 matches) — so a deck that plays more matches (deeper runs) weighs more. Legend identity is read from each decklist's legend slot.
  • Only legends with >30 games are plotted — smaller samples are too noisy to place.
  • Watch zone defaults to >1 SD above the mean in both play and win (auto-computed per scope); the sliders override it.
  • Deep run counts players reaching the chosen match-point total — and match points keep byes, since a bye legitimately earns points toward the Day 2 cut.
  • Everything reflects the selected scope (format or single event). Never pooled across a ban or set release — those are different metagames.

Power rankings · every legend

Sortable. Click a row to inspect domains, staples & trend.

Red row — in the Health-Map watch zone (popular and winning)
Blue row — bottom-band win rate (the weakest decks)
Assumptions & method
  • Win rate = tracked-vs-tracked only (same definition as the Health Map; 50% = average), for the selected scope.
  • Play % = share of submitted decklists. Top 8 = official final placement ≤ 8 (the real tournament result, byes & tiebreakers included).
  • vs field = win rate excluding the mirror (the deck's record against every other legend). It's the truer measure of strength: mirrors are always 50%, so they dilute the plain Win% of popular decks toward 50%. The two diverge most for the most-played decks.
  • Row tint: red = inside the watch zone (play and win above the threshold); blue = bottom-band win rate.

Ban & rotation timeline · where the formats break

Card presence (% of all decks) per event. A card cliffing to 0 mid-set is a ban; one dropping at the legend-pool jump is a rotation. This is how the three formats are defined — and the pre-ban presence levels are the signal that should have triggered review before Bologna.

Is the diversity real? · the “best-of” distortion

The $10–20k best-on-legend foil rewards being the single best pilot of a legend, so players pick under-contested legends — inflating the long tail. Bars compare all effective archetypes vs only the competitively viable ones (≥48% win, ≥20 games) per format. The gap is manufactured diversity.

Winner-meta funnel · what survives and wins

Each legend's share of the field at three stages: what was brought (start of Day 1) → what made the cut (start of Day 2) → what finished 10-3 or better (≥30 match points). Lines that climb are decks that convert — over-represented among the winners; lines that fall fade out. Scoped by Format & Event; the funnel already spans the days, so the Rounds toggle doesn't apply here.

Matchup matrix · the rock-paper-scissors check

Legend-vs-legend win rate from ~10,000 real matches per format (row beats column). This is what aggregate win rate hides: whether the best deck has a counter. Green = row favored, red = row loses; blank = under 10 games. Pick how many legends to show (deeper = more fringe decks with thinner samples). Hover for sample size.

Content reception · how bans and new sets redistribute the player base

The truest measure of a change's reception isn't win rate — it's whether players keep their deck. This follows the global Format / Event scope: pick a format to see the shift from the format before it (the ban wave, or the set rotation), or an event to see what its returning players switched from. Bar = share who kept the same legend.

Learning curve · how fast a format gets “solved”

Win rate can't show learning — it's zero-sum, pinned near 50%. Decklist convergence can: the mean card-list similarity among a legend's pilots. As the community agrees on the optimal build, similarity climbs. One mini-chart per legend (the format's 12 most-played), with the cards behind each move. Follows the Format filter; picking an event shows its format's curve (a curve needs multiple events), and Rounds doesn't apply — decklists are fixed for a whole event.

Similarity = mean pairwise Jaccard of main-deck card sets (0 = all different, 1 = identical). "Locked in" = the biggest inclusion-rate shifts while the build was being solved (first event → its convergence peak); "re-opened" = the shifts after the peak, as lists diverged again. Green = card rose · red = card fell.
